old_title: Ukraine war latest: Putin fires nuclear-capable missile that could reach US
new_title: Ukraine war latest: CIA chief 'proposed Trump-Putin-Zelensky summit'
old_text:
Russia has successfully tested a nuclear-capable intercontinental ballistic missile that could reach the US, its defence ministry has said.
The missile, which has a range of more than 6,700km, was fired from the Arkhangelsk region in the country's northwest and reached its designated target at the Kura test site in Russia's far eastern Kamchatka region.
It comes just days after CIA Director John Ratcliffe had travelled to Moscow to warn Russia off any attack on a NATO member. The Kremlin has said he did not meet president Vladimir Putin during the visit.
Meanwhile, Volodymyr Zelensky has ordered his military to increase its long-range drone strikes against Russia to 1,000 per day, up from around 300 currently.
He also said the US had given Kyiv information about a number of meetings in Moscow over the last few days.
In a Telegram post, he wrote: "Today we received information from the American side about the meetings in Moscow that took place these days. There were a number of meetings there."
In pictures: Aftermath of Russian drone strike on a Kyiv-area warehouse
Ukraine downs 233 Russian drones overnight
Ukraine shot down 233 Russian drones overnight as Moscow continued its wave of attacks,
Its defence force said the drones were struck down across the country.
"Enemy aerial weapons struck 15 locations, while debris from downed drones fell at 4 other sites. Additionally, some enemy munitions failed to reach their targets; information regarding these is currently being verified.
"The attack is ongoing, with several enemy UAVs still in the airspace."
Death toll in Russian attack on Kyiv rises to 37
At least 37 people have been killed following a Russian attack on the Bucha district, close to the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv, officials said Saturday.
Tymur Tkachenko, head of the local regional military administration, said that at least 50 residential buildings had been damaged in the attack, which also sparked a large-scale fire that spread to homes and a restaurant.
Dozens of people have also been injured, officials said.
Volodymyr Zelensky said that a warehouse had been struck in the village of Myla "followed by a detonation."
He did not give details on the site, but wrote in the same message that criminal proceedings had been opened on charges of official negligence.
"There are regulations in place - ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas."
Zelensky vows to punish those responsible for deadly overnight attack
Volodymyr Zelensky has vowed to punish those responsible for the deadly overnight attack on the Kyiv region, which killed at least 27 people.
He said criminal cases had already been opened on charges of official negligence.
The Ukrainian president wrote on X: "Those who allowed this to happen must be held accountable for their decisions.
"There are regulations in place - ammunition cannot be stored near homes or other residential areas. Appropriate conclusions will certainly be drawn."
Dmytrivka community head killed in deadly strike on Kyiv
The head of the Dmytrivka community, which was attacked by Russia overnight, died rescuing people, Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
Taras Didych is one of the 27 people that have been reported killed.
The Ukrainian president said residential buildings, along with a care home for elderly people and people with disabilities, were damaged.
The woman making Ukraine safe from landmines amid a brutal war
Vladimir Putin believes Donald Trump has been "weakened" by the war in Iran and this could allow the Russian president to ramp up aggression in Europe, US intelligence has indicated.
While the details of CIA director John Ratcliffe's trip to Moscow this week remain elusive, The Washington Post has reported that the meeting cautioned Moscow against banking on the US president being distracted by conflict with Tehran to escalate action against Ukraine.
For Putin, the ground war in Ukraine has not proved to be the quick victory he presented to the Russian public, where in 2014, he claimed he could, if he chose to take Kiev, do so "in two weeks."
Instead, as the war drags into its fifth year, Moscow has faced growing levels of internal division, putting pressure on the Russian president.
At least 27 killed in Russian strike on Kyiv region, governor says
At least 27 people were killed after a Russian drone strike on a Kyiv-area warehouse sparked a detonation.
Another 42 people were injured in the overnight Russian air attack, governor Tymur Tkachenko has said.
He said more than 380 were being evacuated from the strike area in the Bucha district, which damaged at least 50 residential buildings and sparked a large-scale fire that spread to homes and a restaurant.
Almost constant air raids in Kyiv have now reached their third day, choking the economy in the Ukrainian capital and severely disrupting civilian life more than 41⁄2 years after Russia's full-scale invasion of its neighbour.

The CIA director floated a summit with Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky, and Donald Trump during his mysterious meeting in Moscow, it is understood.
Two sources briefed on the matter told Axios that John Ratcliffe had spoken to Russian officials this week about a trilateral meeting.
Talks between Ukraine and Russia were paused in February when the US invaded Iran, and little progress has been made since.
Meanwhile, Russia has continued to strike Kyiv with drones overnight after at least 38 people were killed in the deadliest attack on Ukraine's capital this year.
The Ukrainian president vowed to punish those responsible for the deadly attacks, which killed 34 people in a care home for the elderly.
The strikes hit an ammunition depot, sparking a fire in the Bucha district overnight that spread to surrounding areas.
Dozens were injured with nearby infrastructure including residential buildings and the care facility for the elderly and people with disabilities suffering "significant damage".
President Zelensky said cases had already been opened on charges of official negligence.
A look at the deadliest Russian attacks on Ukraine this year
Russia has hit Ukraine with nearly 2,000 drones this week, says Zelensky
Russia has launched nearly 2,000 strike drones, more than 1,600 aerial bombs, and 31 missiles in Ukraine this week, its president said.
Volodymyr Zelensky said strikes were "virtually constant"in Nikopol, Kramatorsk, Kherson, and communities in the Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Donetsk, and Sumy regions.
"We are seeking just responses to every Russian strike and crime. They will certainly come," he said.

Comment: What is the real reason the CIA boss John Ratcliffe made a secret trip to Moscow?
Peter Frankopan writes:
Earlier this week, a C17 Globemaster descended into Moscow's Vnukovo airport. Although it was hopping in from Riga, Latvia, the plane had originated at Andrews Air Force Base, close to Washington DC. On board was John Ratcliffe, the director of the CIA. After being whisked into the Russian capital in a motorcade, a few hours later, Ratcliffe was up in the air again and on his way home.
Who Ratcliffe met was not clear. The visit had not been announced in advance in the US, while Kremlin spokesman Dimitry Peskov claimed to have no knowledge or information about the arrival of a US Air Force plane.
Not surprisingly, there has been much speculation as to why the most senior figure in US intelligence had gone to Moscow in person. After all, if Ratcliffe had an important message to share or communicate, there were other, easier and safer ways to do so than spending hours in a plane travelling to Russia.
Some speculated that Ratcliffe's mission involved Iran, perhaps a request for Moscow's help in focusing Tehran's mind about a workable settlement that might lead to the full re-opening of the Strait of Hormuz, or perhaps a warning that Putin's government should be careful in its dealings with a country that is the focus not only of US military but economic pressure: ties between Russia and Iran have been strong for years, with the latter a source of prodigious numbers of Shahed drones that have been used in the war against Ukraine.
Death toll rises to 38 from Russia's deadliest attack on Ukraine this year
The death toll from Russia's deadly attack on Kyiv rose to 38 with four people still missing, Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday.
The strike on Friday night on the ammunition storage facility sparked massive explosions and fires that swept through dozens of nearby homes and buildings.
The Ukrainian president said twenty people were injured, including two children.
Meanwhile, Russia's defence ministry said on Sunday it is preparing to launch "massive strikes" against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, following a Ukrainian drone campaign against a retailer dubbed "Russia's Amazon" as well as the country's oil and gas sector, which Kyiv says both funds and directly fuels Moscow's invasion of Ukraine.
CIA director proposed Trump, Putin, Zelensky summit - report
The director of the CIA had proposed a meeting between the leaders of Russia, Ukraine, and the US when he visited Moscow, sources say.
During his secret meeting with Russian officials, John Ratcliffe had floated a summit with Vladimir Putin, Volodymyr Zelensky, and Donald Trump, Axios reported.
It comes after talks between Ukraine and Russia were paused in February, when the US invaded Iran.
The US has held talks with negotiators from both sides in recent months, but little progress has been made.
Kyrylo Budanov, Ukraine's head of office, said this week that talks with Russia could resume in September.
Ratcliffe's visit to Moscow on Tuesday, which was not announced in advance, has sparked much speculation.
President Trump played down the visit, saying it was "semi-routine".
Drone attack on Russia's Leningrad region hits residential buildings, sparks fire
Several residential buildings in Russia's Leningrad region were damaged after an attack, governor Alexander Drozdenko has said.
He added that 62 drones had been downed and a fire broke out in an industrial area of the town of Kirishi, but has now been put out.
"The consequences of the fire are currently being assessed," Mr Drozdenko wrote on Telegram.
Russia starts preparations for massive strikes against Ukraine's energy infrastructure, defence ministry says
Moscow has declared it is launching massive strikes on Ukraine's energy facilities in response to attacks on Russian civilian and energy infrastructure.
The Russian defence ministry said on Sunday that preparations for the attacks had begun.
It added that forces had continued overnight to carry out coordinated strikes against Ukraine's defence industry facilities.
Russia continues strikes on Kyiv after dozens killed
Russia has continued its strikes on Ukraine's capital overnight following its deadliest attack on Kyiv this year.
Authorities sent several air-raid alerts as fires were reported across the city, Kyiv Independent reported.
A residential building in Kyiv's Obolonskyi district was reportedly struck by a drone on Saturday night, causing a fire to break out.
Another downed drone was reported in Klitschko, where a fire also broke out.
Two killed, 27 wounded in Russian strikes on Ukraine's Kherson region
Russian strikes hit homes and apartment blocks in the southern Ukrainian region of Kherson on Saturday, killing two people and wounding 27 others, including a child, regional head Oleksandr Prokudin said in a statement.
Mr Prokudin had said earlier in the week that Russia had intensified its attacks on critical infrastructure in the region, about 70 per cent of which is under Russian control.
He urged tens of thousands of residents to move to safer regions, citing the possibility of prolonged power and heating outages this winter.
